item.title: Petit Planet Launches Globally on December 4, With Pre-Download Starting December 1
item.description:
HoYoverse has set the date for the Petit Planet global launch: the cozy life sim opens worldwide on December 4 on iOS, Android and PC, with pre-download starting on December 1.
The date arrived on October 30 with a new trailer on the game’s official channel, closing the “Winter 2026” window the studio had given at gamescom. Pre-registration is still open and comes with exclusive rewards for everyone who signs up before launch.
On PC, Petit Planet will be available through its own Windows client and the Epic Games Store; on mobile, through the App Store and Google Play. Pre-download opens three days early, on December 1, so the game can be installed before the servers go live.
The release date trailer follows a single day on a small planet: a Planet Tender plans a picnic with the Neighbors, picks an outfit, gathers ingredients, cooks a spread of dishes and ends the night around a cake by candlelight, with fireworks over the trees.
In Petit Planet the player becomes a Planet Tender who looks after a planet of their own and watches it grow. The day-to-day loop is farming, fishing, crafting, cooking and exploring the Starsea, while decorating the house and dressing up the character with outfits and accessories.
The planet is shared with the Neighbors, animal and human residents who chat with the player and invite them to gatherings like the picnic, and the game also supports multiplayer. It is HoYoverse’s first life sim, after a final test that ran from September 20.

item.title: IDOLY PRIDE Will End Service in Japan on March 1, 2027, and Become an Offline Game
item.description:
QualiArts has announced the IDOLY PRIDE end of service: the Japanese version of the idol management RPG will shut down on March 1, 2027, and the game will then be updated into an offline version.
The notice went out on the game’s official X account on October 30, 2026. IDOLY PRIDE launched on iOS and Android on June 24, 2021, so the service will close after roughly five years and nine months.
The game stays fully playable until the shutdown, and QualiArts says livestreams and in-game events will keep running during the remaining months. The full schedule of what ends and when is published in the in-game notices.
Players with unused paid currency should keep an eye on the same notices: the application process for a refund of paid Blue Diamonds is explained there.
Instead of disappearing completely, IDOLY PRIDE will receive an update that turns it into an offline version. QualiArts has not yet detailed what that version will keep, so it is not known which story chapters, idols or songs will remain available once the servers go dark.
In the game, the player takes on the role of a manager who forms idol units, clears live performances and guides their idols to the top of the VENUS Program ranking, one of the pieces of the wider IDOLY PRIDE multimedia project.

item.title: Honkai: Star Rail 4.7 Arrives November 11 With Aeon Aha and a Free Limited 5-Star
item.description:
The version also hands every player one limited 5-star of their choice for free — Acheron, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae or Jing Yuan — and introduces a new growth system called Affinitive Eidolon.
For over a thousand Amber Eras, the leviathan known as the Voracity has been kept sealed by Aha’s Phantasmoon Games. Now it is about to wake up, so the Aeon of Elation summons eight Supplicants for the Final Phantasmoon Games and sets sail on the Starfroster, a cake-like ship meant to lure the beast in, with the Trailblazer at their side.
In combat, Aeon ★ Aha is a limited 5-star on the Path of Elation who makes the Path itself ascend, giving every Elation character a unique new ability. Aha also stars in the new Aha Instant, which fast-forwards Elation Skills. The whole team builds up Wishpower during battle, and once it is full Aha’s Ultimate deals Elation damage to all enemies; with their Aeonic Authority, ally attacks can even reduce enemies’ Max HP. The version trailer follows Aha and the Trailblazer into that last performance.
Aeon ★ Aha debuts with Version 4.7. The first half reruns Silver Wolf LV.999, Sparxie and Yao Guang, while the second half brings back Acheron, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae and Jing Yuan, alongside their signature Light Cones Along the Passing Shore, Brighter Than the Sun and Before Dawn.
Those three second-half characters are also the first to get an Affinitive Eidolon: once you own the character and unlock it, they gain new abilities, new animations and character-themed combat buffs. During Version 4.7, logging in lets you pick one Affinitive Eidolon for Acheron, Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae or Jing Yuan.
The main event is The Fluffy Movie: Overheated, where the Trailblazer helps Aha run a dessert shop to earn Gold Coins, and the combat event Interastral Peace Gala: Road to Fame runs at the same time. The Trailblazer Mission also rewards the new 4-star Elation Light Cone See You at the World’s End!
The permanent mode Currency Wars starts its second season, Voyage Into the Canvas, with a full overhaul. Taking part in Phantasia Showstage gives a chance at Aha’s limited outfit Star Lotto, and every reward left in the pool is granted for free once you get it. The animated short A Joyful Funeral Beneath the Moon releases on launch day, and the new track Ex Nihilo accompanies Aha’s final performance.
The three codes from the Version 4.7 Special Program — NEVERGONNAGIVE, NEVERGONNAMAKE and AHABLESSYOU — only work until October 31 at 23:59 (UTC+8), so they have to be redeemed before the update arrives.
Guides, data and news for this game, all in one place.

item.title: KOF: Legend Launches November 4 in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Southeast Asia, Pre-Registration Open
item.description:
KOF: Legend, an idle card RPG licensed by SNK, launches on November 4, 2026 in Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau and Southeast Asia. Pre-registration is open now on the App Store and Google Play. The KOF: Legend release date was announced on October 27 by JOYMAKER GAMES, together with the first gameplay trailer.
It is a different game from Netmarble’s The King of Fighters AFK. KOF: Legend uses 3D models instead of pixel art, and puts the player in the role of a manager who recruits, trains and upgrades fighters from the series.
Every fighter belongs to a faction, and the factions counter each other like rock, paper, scissors: reading the enemy lineup and sending in the fighter who beats it is the core of each battle. Up to three fighters fight on the field at once in real time, and lining up fighters from the same faction activates bonuses. Ultimate cards, chips, the Three Sacred Treasures and equipment complete each build. There are no combos to input: the game is built to be picked up in seconds.
The first five fighters revealed are Kyo Kusanagi (Paper, melee damage), Mai Shiranui (Paper, ranged damage), Iori Yagami (Rock, melee damage), Athena Asamiya (Paper, ranged healer) and Orochi (Rock, ranged damage). Their signature moves are recreated in 3D, from Kyo’s 100 Shiki: Oni Yaki to Iori’s Ya Otome, with the series’ classic music.
The story mode retells the Orochi, NESTS and Ash sagas, and the classic bosses can be recruited for the team: Orochi, Rugal, Clone Zero and Magaki. Players can also team up with two friends against bosses in real time, join a club and take part in 50 vs 50 guild battles.
The gameplay trailer shows the 3D fights and the special moves:
Pre-registration milestones unlock training manuals, diamonds and an Epic fighter chest, all claimed at launch. Inviting friends to form a squad through a personal pre-registration link also unlocks an exclusive manager outfit.

item.title: BanG Dream! Our Notes Data Leak in Japan Exposes Details of Over 13,000 Beta Applicants and Support Users
item.description:
Bushiroad has confirmed a BanG Dream! Our Notes data leak in Japan. A third party broke into the systems of a company contracted to develop the game, and took the personal data of 10,194 people who applied for the closed beta and 3,034 people who contacted customer support.
The official notice, published on October 27, 2026, covers the Japanese version of the rhythm game, which Bushiroad operates. Those affected will be contacted individually.
The closed beta ran from June 25 to June 29, 2026. For each of the 10,194 applicants, the leak includes the email address used to apply, the IP address at the time of applying, the date and time of the application and the type of device (iOS or Android, without the OS version). Bushiroad says that, so far, no names, addresses, phone numbers, passwords or credit card details have been found among the leaked data.
Data on 71 people who worked on the beta also leaked, along with 5 survey answers that contained personal details: four email addresses and one X account.
The second batch covers every inquiry sent to customer support between September 24 at 14:03 and October 14 at 23:46, the first three weeks after launch. The leaked messages include their full text, and depending on what each player wrote, other details:
Bushiroad says a player ID on its own is not enough to log into an account, take it over or change its data.
The cause was a management flaw at the contractor, which has since been fixed. Bushiroad has found no unauthorized access beyond those storage environments and no secondary damage, but it warns that fake emails or text messages pretending to come from the company or the game may appear. Players should not open links or attachments in messages they do not recognize: Bushiroad never asks for passwords, card details or bank PINs by email or SMS, and never requests payment directly.
The company says it will review the contractor’s security and tighten the handling of personal data across the whole group, and will publish any new facts it finds.

item.title: BLEACH Mirrors High Is Out Now on iOS and Android, With Sosuke Aizen in the First Banner
item.description:
BLEACH Mirrors High is out now on the App Store and Google Play. Bandai Namco’s new mobile game for the anime went live worldwide on October 28, 2026 (UTC) after the launch maintenance, and its first banner features [Standing at the Top] Sosuke Aizen.
The game is free-to-play with in-app purchases. Its story begins after BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War, with the player as a Soul Reaper of their own, a customizable appearance and Zanpakuto, and a cast of new recruits designed by series creator Tite Kubo.
Aizen was revealed during the SPECIAL BROADCAST on October 27, in a trailer narrated by his Japanese voice actor, Sho Hayami. He is a 4-star character, and his banner runs from launch until November 24, 2026 at 14:59 (UTC+9).
He joins the 13 characters of the launch lineup: Ichigo Kurosaki, Rukia Kuchiki, Byakuya Kuchiki, Renji Abarai, Toshiro Hitsugaya, Rangiku Matsumoto, Mayuri Kurotsuchi, Yoruichi Shihoin, Uryu Ishida, Orihime Inoue, Yasutora Sado, Grimmjow Jeagerjaques and Bambietta Basterbine.
The broadcast also revealed the full cast of the 15 new recruits. The two leads are Shirin Migishima, voiced by Chiaki Kobayashi, and Shirane Sanari, voiced by Maria Sashide. They train alongside the player and fight next to the original Soul Reapers in a story that picks up after the war against the Quincy.
Battles are card-based. Players lead a squad of three, pick Chain, Arts and Skill cards each turn, building up to special attacks staged like the anime.
For the BLEACH Mirrors High release, Bandai Namco published an opening animation made by PIERROT FILMS, the studio behind the Thousand-Year Blood War anime. It plays over the theme song “CRITICAL” by suisoh, arranged with Takahiro Yamada of ASIAN KUNG-FU GENERATION:
Returning characters such as Ichigo and Rukia keep their original Japanese voice actors.

item.title: DIGIMON ALYSION Opens Pre-Registration, Bringing the Digimon Card Game to iOS and Android
item.description:
BANDAI has opened DIGIMON ALYSION pre-registration on the App Store and Google Play. The free-to-play app brings the Digimon Card Game to smartphones with nearly the same rules as the physical game, an original story and new cards made only for the app. There is no release date yet.
The game is coming to players worldwide, with text in English, Japanese, Korean and Chinese. Cards are obtained from packs: there is one free pack every day, and the collection includes Shiny Cards, Alt-Art Cards and animated Premium Alt-Art Cards alongside the cards already printed for the paper game.
The official pre-registration campaign runs until launch and unlocks rewards as the player count grows. They arrive by in-game mail on release day:
Matches follow the rules of the paper game. Players build a deck of exactly 50 cards plus a Digi-Egg deck of up to 5, with a limit of 4 copies of each card. The goal is to break through the opponent’s 5 security cards and then attack them directly. Stacking cards to digivolve a Digimon activates its inherited effects, and each card played pushes the shared memory counter towards the other side: once it crosses over, the turn ends.
What changes is the handling. The app tracks costs, unsuspends cards and resolves card effects automatically, and a tutorial built into the story teaches the rules to players who have never touched the card game. There are ranked matches against players from around the world, friendly matches, and a breeding mode where Digimon are raised up to Mega to fill a Digidex of more than 100 entries.
The campaign follows Kanata, a veteran gamer who has always loved Digimon but never played with the cards. Her online friend Futre invites her to DIGIMON LIBERATOR, a hugely popular online card game played in full-dive VR, and the two head into the metaverse space LACUNA, where Kanata meets new friends and rivals.
The pre-registration trailer shows the story scenes, card battles and the new Digimon designed for the app:
DIGIMON ALYSION held a closed beta in 2025 and is free-to-play with in-app purchases.

item.title: Destiny Child: Assemble Announced by Com2uS as an Idle RPG for First Half of 2027
item.description:
Destiny Child is coming back. Com2uS has revealed Destiny Child: Assemble, a new idle RPG based on SHIFT UP’s series, and opened its teaser site on October 27, 2026, the year of the original game’s 10th anniversary. It is set to launch globally on iOS and Android in the first half of 2027.
With Destiny Child: Assemble announced, the series gets a new game three years after the original closed in 2023. Development is in the hands of TikiTaka Studio, a Com2uS subsidiary, while Com2uS handles global publishing. The deal for the rights to the IP was signed in November 2024.
The original Destiny Child, released by SHIFT UP in 2016, was a character collector known for its roster of more than 500 Childs and for being animated in Live2D across the whole game. Assemble keeps that focus: it is designed around collecting and growing characters, with each Child’s story woven into that progression.
On the narrative side, the game will carry over the original scenario and side stories and add new story content. The subtitle refers to the players themselves: in the first game they were the Archfiend candidates, and “Assemble” is about them gathering once again.
The 25-second teaser centers on the Resurrection Flower, the holy relic from the original lore that brings things back to life, with lines that hint at a reunion. The teaser site is available in English, Korean and Japanese.
Teaser Video Released. The time to reunite is drawing near.
The official X account will also publish a series of four-panel comics about the game’s development, and Com2uS has said more details will follow through the website and its social channels.

item.title: Pokémon UNITE Will End Service on March 23, 2027
item.description:
Pokémon UNITE is shutting down worldwide. The Pokémon Company has confirmed that the team battle game will end service on Tuesday, March 23, 2027, at 00:00 UTC, on both Nintendo Switch and mobile, after more than five and a half years online.
The Pokémon UNITE end of service was announced on October 27, 2026 in an official notice. The game, developed by TiMi Studio Group, launched on Switch on July 21, 2021 and reached iOS and Android that September.
The wind-down started the same day as the announcement. Since October 27 at 05:00 UTC, Aeos gems can no longer be bought, although players can keep spending the ones they already have until the servers close.
On November 12, 2026, at 04:00 UTC, an update adds a Unite Coin Exchange. Special Unite coins, earned through a log-in bonus and missions completed by winning ranked matches and other battle modes, can be traded for items that have appeared in the game before: Unite licenses, Holowear, Trainer fashion and Unite snapshot items.
The same update brings a library feature. It lets players visit the Practice Area and look back at their Holowear, Unite licenses, emblems, achievements and tournament results, and it keeps working after the shutdown, but only for those who have downloaded its data before March 23, 2027. The download happens while playing normally or when opening the feature for the first time, and the data generally cannot be moved to a new device.
The competitive scene gets one last season. The Pokémon UNITE Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo tournament will still be held as planned, with qualifiers starting on December 5, 2026.
After March 23, 2027, players will no longer be able to log in or join battles. Support stays open for any issues until the servers close.

item.title: Brave Frontier LEGION Opens Global Pre-Registration on iOS and Android
item.description:
Brave Frontier LEGION is coming west: Brave Frontier LEGION pre-registration for the global version opened on October 26, 2026 on the App Store and Google Play. The online co-op battle RPG from GrandSoft, built on gumi’s Brave Frontier series, has been live in Japan since July 22, 2025.
The global edition is published by ALPSE PTE. LTD., and its English store listings and official website are already up. A launch date has not been announced yet.
The core of LEGION is the Legion Battle: co-op clashes where up to ten players on each side fight together, coordinating through chat and stickers to climb the rankings. Outside those fights, players build decks of Units and train them until they reach new Evolution forms, as in the original Brave Frontier.
Battles run in full-auto, with flashy Brave Burst skill animations doing the work, so a session fits into a few spare minutes. The global listing promises up to 1,000 Summons for taking part in Legion Battles.
Pre-registration for the global version of BRAVE FRONTIER LEGION is now open!
The Japanese version keeps running alongside it, with new units still arriving.
